instruction: Flatten One Side of a Sphere Using ClipCurve The opened `scene.obj` contains a ZBrush Tool whose first (and only) SubTool, named Sphere, is a standard polygonal sphere of radius 1.0 BU centred at the Tool's origin, with approximately 3,000-10,000 faces. The surface is perfectly spherical: every vertex lies at radius 1.0 +/- 1e-4. The SubTool has no polygroups beyond the default, no UVs, and no polypaint. Using the opened OBJ in ZBrush, use the ClipCurve brush to shear off the right-hand half of the sphere, everything with x > 0 in world space, so that the resulting shape is a half-sphere whose flat face lies on the YZ plane (x = 0), and export the result as `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.obj`. The exported `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.obj` must satisfy: - Exactly one SubTool, still named Sphere. - Every vertex has x <= 0.001 BU. - At least 100 vertices lie within x in [-0.01, 0.001], forming the flat cap, and their maximum |x| is <= 0.002. - Vertices with x < -0.5 have moved by less than 0.001 BU from their original positions. - The mesh is manifold.
